question: Who was the founder of the Tattwabodhini Sabha, a reformist movement in Bengal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Debendranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Debendranath Tagore** founded the Tattwabodhini Sabha in Bengal in **1839**.
 
• The Sabha aimed to **revive the principles of the Brahmo Samaj**, emphasizing monotheism and the Upanishadic philosophy.
 
• The Tattwabodhini Sabha became a hub for discussions on **social and religious reforms** in Bengal.
 
• It also played a significant role in promoting **Bengali language and literature** by publishing the "Tattwabodhini Patrika," a journal that propagated reformist ideas.
 
• Debendranath Tagore, often referred to as the **"Maharshi,"** was a key figure in the Bengal Renaissance and contributed significantly to the intellectual awakening in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**

 
 
• Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828, it was a socio-religious reform movement that opposed idol worship and emphasized monotheism.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj sought to reform Hinduism by eliminating practices like sati, caste discrimination, and child marriage.
 
 
 
• **Tattwabodhini Patrika:**
 
 
• This journal was the official publication of the Tattwabodhini Sabha.
 
• It served as a medium to disseminate the Sabha's reformist ideas and foster intellectual debates.
 
 
 
• **Debendranath Tagore:**
 
 
• He was the father of Rabindranath Tagore, a Nobel laureate in literature.
 
• He joined the Brahmo Samaj in 1843 and later played a pivotal role in its revival.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Renaissance:**
 
 
• A cultural, social, and intellectual awakening in 19th-century Bengal, spearheaded by luminaries like Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Debendranath Tagore.
 
• It aimed to reform traditional Indian society by adopting progressive ideas while retaining the essence of Indian culture.
